subject: english
question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.**

I assisted him to undo the (task after I finished my work).

options.text: task after I had finished my work
task after I will finish my work
task after I will have finished my work

solution:
The correct answer is **"task after I had finished my work."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reason to use **"task after I had finished my work"** is to maintain proper verb tense consistency.
 
• In this case**, "I had finished"** is in the past perfect tense, which is appropriate because it indicates an action completed before another past action (assisting him to undo the task).
 
• This construction helps to clarify the sequence of events in the past. 
 
• The correct answer is option 1.

 

**Correct sentence**: *I assisted him to undo the **task after I had finished my work**__.*
